decisive_kills.reason: Current paid SDK-maintenance work explicitly cites the 2026-07-28 session rewrite and has hired engineers at $60-$90/hour, so spec churn does create paid engineering demand. Evidence does not show a broad standalone buyer pool for a separate migration operator.

The official MCP release includes a minimum twelve-month deprecation policy and modern infrastructure supports dual-era negotiation. Earlier protocol implementations remain in real use; this is migration work, not a universal immediate cutover deadline.

Within weeks of the revision, multiple independent specialists already publish fixed-price readiness audits and migration sprints, including MCP Migration Studio, Accura.dev, Stratt Labs and ECZ-ID Trust MCP. The category is early but supply is no longer demonstrably sparse.

Free remote probes can test protocol negotiation and surface behavior, but they explicitly cannot inspect session-keyed application state, OAuth/protected-resource correctness, long-lived flows or hidden error paths. The official TypeScript guide likewise says 2026-07-28 adoption is architectural and not codemod-automatable.

Official SDKs ship detailed migration guidance and agent-oriented codemods; Cloudflare servers and portals already negotiate the 2026-07-28 revision alongside older clients, and AWS AgentCore documents dual-version gateway support. The reusable conformance layer is rapidly becoming SDK/gateway/tool functionality.

Reusable public protocol rules and conformance probes are easy to copy and increasingly available as free/open tooling. The difficult residual knowledge lives in each customer's private source, auth topology and deployment state, which cannot be reused as a cross-customer asset.
Provider landing pages prove sellers are positioning for the work, not that a new operator can acquire enough high-intent migration buyers organically without recurring founder-led sales.

evidence.title: The 2026-07-28 Specification
evidence.fact: Largest MCP revision since launch; stateless core plus a formal minimum twelve-month deprecation policy.

evidence.title: Supporting protocol revision 2026-07-28
evidence.fact: Existing v2 code does not automatically speak the new revision; migration requires explicit changes.

evidence.title: MCP TypeScript SDK migration guides
evidence.fact: The official v1-to-v2 path includes a codemod and is structured for LLM-agent use, while 2026-07-28 adoption remains architectural rather than fully codemod-automatable.
